items.prompt: Construct a ≤5-state PDA for 0ᵐ1ᵐ⁺ⁿ0ⁿ, m,n≥1; satisfy normalization conditions already.
items.guide: Separate the first matched 0/1 block from the later matched 1/0 block. The middle phase can pop old zero markers then push markers for trailing zeros. Show the three preconditions.

items.prompt: Convert that PDA to CFG wrapped rules; give push/pop tables.
items.guide: Pair each push with every pop of the same stack symbol; include the bottom-marker pair. Only the wrapped family is requested.

items.prompt: Construct a ≤2-state PDA for 0ᵐ1ⁿ, m≥n≥0, with Γ={0}; give diagram and formal definition.
items.guide: Push on zeros; switch on the first one and pop on ones. Both ordinary phases accept because leftover zeros and ε are allowed.

items.prompt: Prove no one-state PDA with Γ={0} recognizes that language.
items.guide: Use acceptance of ε and 01, then replay an accepting 01 run to force acceptance of 0101. Explain why stack operations remain legal.

items.prompt: Construct a ≤3-state DPDA, including reject state; give δ.
items.guide: Remove choices, retain both accepting phases, reject zeros after ones, and check all four-way table conditions.

items.prompt: Simulate the supplied PDA on 000111 using a tree.
items.guide: Keep branches for the competing 1 transitions with different stack effects. A single path is explicitly insufficient.

items.prompt: Find a counterexample to that PDA for 0ᵐ1ⁿ, m≤n, and draw its tree.
items.guide: Check zero-only inputs and too few ones; acceptance in an ordinary state need not empty the stack. The paper supplies 0 and 001 as examples.

items.prompt: Repair the PDA using ≤4 states and one accept state; trace the counterexample.
items.guide: Use a bottom-marker check before final acceptance; preserve ε and strings containing only ones.

items.prompt: Convert S→A|0A, A→SAS|ε to CNF, showing all four stages.
items.guide: Track both nullable S occurrences and the induced A→S unit rule. The full worked lesson follows this question.

items.prompt: Design a ≤9-state outside-in TM for w#wᴿ with restricted Γ; trace 01#10 and 010#0 fully.
items.guide: Remember the erased left bit in the state; find and erase the matching rightmost bit. Check # and exhaustion on both sides; count both halting states.

items.prompt: Use the prescribed inside-out TM strategy with ≤8 states and special initial-symbol marks; trace both strings.
items.guide: Use the left boundary marks to know when matching is complete; verify extra separators and the string #. Follow the specified strategy.

items.prompt: Give a ≤4-state two-tape TM for the same reversal language and trace both strings.
items.guide: Copy the left side to tape 2, then compare the right side while scanning that copy backwards. Show both head positions at each joint step.

items.prompt: Adapt the square-length pumping proof using i=3 and the lecture witness.
items.guide: With |y|=k, bound the new length p²+2k strictly between p² and (p+1)².

items.prompt: Can the same witness use i=0 if square lengths exclude n=0?
items.guide: Treat p≥2 by adjacent-square bounds; treat p=1 separately, where ε is now outside the language.

items.prompt: Give the full truth table for ¬(A∧B∧C) and (A∧B)⇒¬C.
items.guide: Write eight rows. Both formulas are false only when A,B,C are all true.

items.prompt: Decide regularity for nonempty binary strings with average bit value ≤0.9; explicitly give s and i.
items.guide: Use a boundary ratio such as 1⁹ᵖ0ᵖ, then add only ones. Cover all legal loop lengths, including |y|=p.

items.prompt: Decide regularity of 0ʰ1ᵏ with h>5k and positive h,k.
items.guide: Choose s=0⁵ᵖ⁺¹1ᵖ and delete a nonempty zero-only loop. The strict inequality then fails.

items.prompt: Construct a ≤2-state PDA for binary strings whose number of ones is divisible by six; formal definition required.
items.guide: Store nonzero remainders in the stack alphabet and use the accepting control state for remainder zero. Zero symbols leave the remainder unchanged.

items.prompt: Give a CFG for the same language with ≤5 rules and ≤3 variables.
items.guide: Generate groups of six ones with arbitrary zero blocks in every gap; include the all-zero/empty case. Count alternatives as specified.

items.prompt: Convert S→CS|ε, C→SCS|CS|1 to CNF with stages.
items.guide: S is nullable. Both occurrences in SCS matter; remove C→C and induced units. The second worked task covers this grammar.

items.prompt: Identify the language of the supplied PDA and explain it.
items.guide: The marker stack matches halves by length; a forced 1 must appear in the second half. Distinguish this from matching the halves symbol by symbol.

items.prompt: Normalize the PDA without changing Σ or Γ; construct all CFG rule families.
items.guide: Replace the no-stack-change edge by a matched push/pop through an intermediate state. Include wrapped, concatenation, and empty rules; do not add a forbidden stack symbol.

items.prompt: Convert hamburger grammar H→bCb, C→mC|CbC|ε into a PDA by the prescribed procedure.
items.guide: Push production right sides in reverse order, include terminal-matching loops and the bottom-marker finish.

items.prompt: Convert that grammar to CNF with the prescribed stages.
items.guide: C is nullable in several positions; CbC creates Cb, bC and b. Isolate b,m in longer right sides and binarize.

items.prompt: Determine ambiguity of bmbmb in that grammar.
items.guide: Give two complete leftmost derivations, differing in whether the outer C first uses mC or CbC.

items.prompt: Prove 0.5n≤m≤1.5n iff n choices from {1,2,3} can sum to 2m.
items.guide: One direction is a bound on the sum. The other needs an explicit choice of counts of 1s/2s or 2s/3s, including n=0.

items.prompt: Complete the specified ≤7-state PDA with Γ={0,$} using that idea.
items.guide: Push two markers per zero; nondeterministically pop one to three per one; accept exactly when the bottom marker is reached.

items.prompt: Draw full simulation trees for 001 and 011.
items.guide: The first rejects, the second accepts. Include all nondeterministic pop choices, not merely the successful path.

items.prompt: Read the language of the supplied two-state PDA.
items.guide: Recognize that accepting final states permit unused stack markers: m≥n, not m=n.

items.prompt: Normalize it using ≤6 states and a stack alphabet of at most three symbols.
items.guide: Use a separate drain path rather than adding free pops to active computation states; then repair any no-op stack move.

items.prompt: Give wrapped CFG rules and push/pop tables for the normalized machine.
items.guide: Account for original matching pops, drain pops, bottom-marker pops, and any dummy-symbol pair.

items.prompt: Construct a ≤4-state PDA for strings containing 01101, using Σ=Γ={0,1}.
items.guide: Use state plus stack-top combinations to encode progress along the fixed pattern, then consume any suffix in an accepting phase.

items.prompt: Define an equivalent NFA for a PDA with a uniform bound m on stack cells.
items.guide: States are (control state, stack string of length ≤m). Start with empty stack; accepting pairs have accepting control states. Define both pop and no-pop transition cases.

items.prompt: Give a ≤7-state two-tape TM computing x⊗y from x#y while restoring tape 1; follow alphabet restrictions.
items.guide: Remember the current bit of x on tape 2 while scanning y, emit the product block, then restore that bit in its marked tape-1 position.

items.prompt: Simulate on 01#10 with joint tape configurations.
items.guide: The output is 0010 and tape 1 must end unchanged. Only movement-only sequences may be compressed as the question permits.

items.prompt: Identify the languages of B,D,X in the supplied grammar.
items.guide: B yields b*, D yields c*, and X yields aⁱbⁱ for i≥1. Explain bases and recursive contributions.

items.prompt: Use those results to identify the languages of Y and S in detail.
items.guide: Y equates a/c counts with at least one pair; S unions that branch with the a/b-equality branch and free trailing cs.

items.prompt: Determine ambiguity of a²b²c².
items.guide: Use two leftmost derivations through the XD and Y start branches.

items.prompt: Convert the grammar to CNF in the specified nullable/unit order.
items.guide: D and B can disappear; add the induced alternatives before removing units. Retain all conditions while introducing helpers.

items.prompt: Convert the simplified S→Y, Y→aBc|aYc, B→bB|ε grammar into a PDA.
items.guide: Use stack substitutions in reverse order and matching loops for a,b,c. The hint expects nine nodes.

items.prompt: Complete the fixed PDA for positive block lengths a,b,c forming an arithmetic progression.
items.guide: Use a+c=2b. Two pops per 1 cancel initial markers; after the bottom is reached, two pushes per remaining 1 prepare the final block. Handle odd/even leftover phases.

items.prompt: Draw simulation trees for 012 and 00112.
items.guide: 012 accepts; 00112 fails the count relation. Preserve mandatory positive blocks and all transition branches.

items.prompt: Identify the language of the supplied PDA.
items.guide: One 1 accounts for up to two zeros; include odd zero counts and zero zeros. The language is 0ᵐ1ⁿ with n≥m/2 and nonnegative counts.

items.prompt: Repair a no-op stack transition without changing states or alphabets.
items.guide: Replace the final-state loop with a push followed by an already available matching pop, preserving input consumption.

items.prompt: Give all wrapped rules with matching-symbol pairing tables.
items.guide: Cross every push with every matching pop, including less obvious paths through reused states.

items.prompt: Explain why the original PDA is not deterministic.
items.guide: Exhibit an actual four-way conflict between a zero push and an ε bottom-marker pop.

items.prompt: Modify the original into a DPDA without changing Q,Σ,Γ; complete δ and F.
items.guide: Remove the conflict while separately preserving ε and all-one inputs. Complete missing combinations with qᵣ as required.

items.prompt: Design the prescribed ≤6-state TM matching adult/child boarding and exit events.
items.guide: Mark the first cell F, remember event type in state, find a later matching exit, mark it ×, and return. Respect prefix feasibility and empty input.

items.prompt: Trace the TM on A+A+A−A− to halting.
items.guide: Show each state, tape edit, and head position through the final accept transition.

items.prompt: Give leftmost derivations of jjb and bbbb in the supplied grammar.
items.guide: Always expand the leftmost variable; ε vanishes from the resulting string.

items.prompt: Decide whether j is ambiguous in that grammar.
items.guide: A nullable B may disappear directly or split into two nullable Bs, giving distinct leftmost derivations.

items.prompt: Convert to CNF with the exact requested ε and unit removal order.
items.guide: Track B,J,S nullability and preserve S₀→ε. Show the intermediate grammars, not just the final normal form.

items.prompt: Complete the provided CFG-to-PDA draft without adding states.
items.guide: Match each long production to its reverse-push chain, sharing only compatible remaining pushes.

items.prompt: Fill the PDA δ table from the supplied diagram for 0ᵐ1ⁿ0ⁿ.
items.guide: Each nonempty output is a set of (state,push) pairs. Read the input and pop fields separately.

items.prompt: Fill the modified DPDA table including reject completion.
items.guide: Use single pairs instead of singleton sets. Check the four potentially applicable entries for each actual input/top combination.

items.prompt: Draw the full simulation tree on 01112.
items.guide: Track both the state and ordered stack through the phase boundaries and ε pop moves.

items.prompt: Explain the language of the supplied seven-state PDA.
items.guide: The first component matches m zeros with m ones, m>0; the second matches 2n additional ones with n twos, n≥0.

items.prompt: Identify failed normalization conditions; repair using the same Q,Σ,Γ and resimulate.
items.guide: The no-stack-change edge is the issue. A permitted push followed by a matching pop can preserve the phase change without extra states.

items.prompt: Convert the normalized PDA to wrapped CFG rules with pairing tables.
items.guide: Group by Δ₁,Δ₂,$ and enumerate the Cartesian product of pushes and pops for each symbol.

items.prompt: Complete the ≤9-state binary-to-quaternary TM for even-length x# by the given five-step algorithm.
items.guide: Process each two-bit pair as 2xᵢ+xᵢ₊₁, erase its source cells and append one base-four digit. The example bit string 11011000 represents decimal 216; the paper’s 213 label is inconsistent.

items.prompt: Fully simulate on 11#.
items.guide: It should finish with two blanks, #, and output digit 3. Show all return scans and the halting transition.

items.prompt: Give leftmost derivations of ghgghg and gg in the supplied grammar.
items.guide: Track the leftmost remaining variable and nullable G,H carefully. A derivation is an ordered sequence, not a list of rules used.

items.prompt: Determine ambiguity of ghg with reasons.
items.guide: Compare the gG and HhGg start branches and produce two complete leftmost derivations.

items.prompt: Perform only the first three CNF stages, following the specified removal order.
items.guide: Do exactly the requested stages; the problem explicitly omits binarization and terminal replacement. Repeated H occurrences create multiple nullable alternatives.

items.prompt: Convert the CFG to the fixed PDA draft, sharing states as needed.
items.guide: Reverse-push chains with identical suffix work can merge. Check that sharing does not create an unintended production.

items.prompt: Draw the full simulation tree for 1010 in the supplied PDA.
items.guide: Preserve guesses at the inner-block boundary; the accepted branch ends with empty working stack and complete input.

items.prompt: Identify the PDA language using reverse and bit-flip notation.
items.guide: The inner and outer stacks match reversed, flipped symbols. The outer pushed block ends in 1; the inner pushed block starts and ends in 0. Watch the overbars in the PDF: text extraction drops them.

items.prompt: Give wrapped CFG rules and tables for all five stack symbols.
items.guide: There are nine push/pop pairings: one for Δ₁, two for Δ₂, four for Δ₃, one for Δ₄ and one for $.

items.prompt: Build a ≤6-state PDA validating the specified $$$ comment syntax.
items.guide: Track opening/closing delimiter counts and require the newline immediately after closing. Distinguish ordinary text from comment content and respect Γ.

items.prompt: Show an accepting path for a$$$b$$$△.
items.guide: This subpart requests a path, not a full tree. Include stack updates for all six dollar symbols and the required newline.

items.prompt: Design the ≤11-state masking TM following the supplied procedure and input promise.
items.guide: Keep the current a/b in control states, find its mask bit, append only on 1, and return through the two separators.

items.prompt: Fully simulate on ab#01# through halting.
items.guide: The output is b after the second #; both input and mask positions are erased. The worked simulator uses the official diagram’s transitions.
